temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Small wedges, from small potatoes 390°F / 200°C · 16 min 425°F / 220°C · 23 min Medium, potato cut in 8 390°F / 200°C · 20 min 425°F / 220°C · 29 min Large, potato cut in 6 390°F / 200°C · 25 min 425°F / 220°C · 36 min Brown outside, dense inside A wedge is thick at the skin side and sharp at the inner edge, so it cooks unevenly by shape alone. The thin point browns first while the heart of the wedge, often more than an inch across, is still firm and waxy. Unlike a thin fry, a wedge has enough bulk that the outside can look done long before the middle is. Two things fix it. First, give each wedge room: wedges stacked in a basket shade each other and the hidden faces steam, so the outside is soft in some places and burnt in others. Second, turn them once onto the other cut face, so both flat sides colour against the basket while the skin side faces the fan. For a really fluffy centre, simmer the wedges for five minutes before they go in. Worked example Two medium russets, each cut lengthways into eight wedges, dried, tossed with a tablespoon of oil, salt, garlic powder and paprika. Cook in a single layer, skin side down, at 390°F for 20 minutes, turning once halfway. Wedges cut from small potatoes take about 16 minutes; chunky sixths about 25. On a baking tray in a conventional oven, plan on 425°F for about 29 minutes. How to tell they are done Push a knife into the thickest part, near the skin: it should slide in with no resistance, and the inside should look white and fluffy rather than glassy. The cut faces should be golden with darker edges and the skin wrinkled and crisp. If the outside is ready and the centre is not, lower the heat a little for the last few minutes rather than giving up the crust. Before they go in Use floury potatoes for a fluffy middle; waxy ones give a firmer, creamier wedge. Scrub but do not peel. Cut every potato into the same number of wedges so they finish together. A short rinse is enough; dry them well. Grated parmesan in the last two minutes is a good addition. Related presets Baked potato 400°F · 40 min · flip at 20 Homemade fries 380°F · 18 min · shake ×2 Broccoli 375°F · 8 min · shake ×1 425°F oven to air fryer, every food → Oven to air fryer converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How long do potato wedges take in the air fryer? About 20 minutes at 390°F for medium wedges, turned once. Small wedges take around 16 minutes and large ones around 25. Should I parboil wedges before air frying? It is optional. Five minutes in simmering water gives a fluffier centre and a rougher surface that crisps more; dry them well afterwards. How are wedges different from fries in the air fryer? Wedges are much thicker, so the challenge is cooking the centre before the outside overbrowns. They need more time and only one turn. Which potatoes make the best wedges? Russets or other floury potatoes for a fluffy inside; Yukon Gold for a creamier one. What is the oven equivalent for potato wedges? 425°F for around 29 minutes on a tray in a conventional oven, or 400°F for 22 minutes in a fan oven.
